players.name: Bullhorn
players.summary: Incumbent recruitment CRM/ATS with a large partner marketplace and agency base.
reasons: Bullhorn holds years of candidate, job, client and placement records from thousands of agencies, and sells insights built on them. It stops at 7 because I could not independently confirm how exclusive that data is.
Agencies run their daily work in it: candidates, jobs, clients and invoicing. Moving all of that elsewhere is slow and risky, so it scores near the top.
A large, established company with a published GDPR commitment and enterprise customers. I held it at 6 because I did not confirm a full list of audited certificates.
The biggest installed base in recruitment software, plus a partner network that recommends it. Agencies find it without Bullhorn starting from zero.

Bullhorn has a large partner marketplace, which is the strongest ecosystem in this list. The '300+ partners' figure is Bullhorn's own and I have not checked the whole list. Bullhorn's partner programme pages.
Some effect through the marketplace, but each agency's data stays separate, so 4.
Software only.
Its size spreads cost across a huge customer base, and it now owns Textkernel too.
players.evidence: Bullhorn home page, GDPR commitment statement and partner programme FAQ. My first score of 54 was too high, so I re-audited it down to 51.

tech.sources: Each customer's own ATS/CRM records plus 26 years of placement data for Search & Match. Bullhorn Insights sells separate labour-market data.
tech.collection: No scraping described. 10,000+ customers, 300+ marketplace partners.
tech.processing: Amplify Chat, described as a staffing LLM (vendor not named). Digital workers with skills to enrich, match, screen, prospect, transcribe and verify.
tech.output: Ranked candidates, outreach, scored interviews, updated records, chat that can take actions.

players.name: Textkernel Market IQ
players.summary: Labour-market data and parsing, owned by Bullhorn since its acquisition.
reasons: It reads and structures very large volumes of CVs and job ads, so it holds labour-market data few rivals have. Most of what I know comes from its own pages, so I did not go above 8.
Its parser sits inside ATS and recruiter workflows, but it is a component that can be swapped, so 6.
An established company with security claims and Bullhorn behind it. I did not confirm a full audited-certificate list, so 6.
Textkernel can now sell to Bullhorn's large customer base, which is a major channel. Bullhorn acquired Textkernel, reported by Staffing Industry Analysts.
It plugs into many ATS and HR systems. After checking the integrations page my first score came down, because I could name fewer partners than its claim suggested.
Each customer's use does not help the others much, so 3.
Software only.
Large processing volume helps its cost, but those scale figures are its own claims, so 6.
players.evidence: Textkernel's English site (94 pages), its integrations page and press coverage of the Bullhorn acquisition. I re-audited it from 48 down to 44.

tech.sources: Job ads crawled from company sites and job boards: 3 billion+ current and historical postings from 33 million+ websites in 15 markets.
tech.collection: Crawls millions of sites continuously in NA, Europe and APAC.
tech.processing: Extracts 50+ data points per job, de-duplicates, normalises to taxonomies, and uses deep learning to separate agencies from direct employers.
tech.output: Market IQ portal (job leads, organisations, insights), alerts, API and data feeds into ATS/CRM.
tech.pricing: Jobfeed from €100/mo; Market IQ on request.

Zoho publishes a long list of compliance certifications and is a large, long-established company, so this is strong.
Zoho sells to its huge existing suite customer base and has a well-known brand, which brings recruiters in cheaply.
A large Zoho marketplace and many integrations make this strong.
Each customer works alone, so 2.
Zoho is known to run its own data centres, which gives it some physical advantage over a software-only rival.
The parent company's size lowers its running costs, but recruitment is a small part of it, so 6.
players.evidence: Zoho's compliance page, About page and Recruit pages. Re-audited from 43 down to 42.

tech.sources: Only data recruiters and candidates enter. Zoho says it does not scrape outside data.

players.name: Exa
players.summary: Search API for AI agents, usable as infrastructure for signal discovery.

Exa has passed an outside security audit, which most startups have not. Its Trust Center (on Vanta) confirms SOC 2 Type II and a HIPAA attestation. One catch: zero data retention is a paid extra, while the home page suggests it is standard.
Strong attention from developers and AI companies. Most of the reach figures are Exa's own, so 6.
Many AI tools and frameworks connect to Exa, so 7.
One customer's use does not improve it for others, so 2.
It runs its own search infrastructure and computing, which is costly to copy.
Its index and computing scale help its costs, but the figures are mostly its own, so 5.

tech.sources: Its own web index: claims 2 trillion URLs tracked and 100 billion documents in its vector database.

tech.output: Search API results with highlights and citations; Websets lists of people or companies exported to CSV, Clay or a CRM. Hosted MCP server.

Customers simply copy Vela on an email thread, so it fits the way recruiters already work. The same ease means it is also easy to stop using. The home page and YC launch post say 'no dashboard, no new workflow'. It works over email, SMS, WhatsApp, calendars and Zoom, and handles reschedules and cancellations.

Vela shows a security logo but gives no proof of it. There is no certificate, no report and no Trust Center, so I treated the claim as unconfirmed. The home page shows an AICPA SOC logo with no text or link. The privacy notice, contract and terms never mention SOC 2, ISO or any certification, and no subprocessor list exists. Only a 99.5% uptime target is stated.

Vela has a good launch channel in Y Combinator and some well-known customers, and every email it sends shows its name to new people. All customer results are its own claims. Y Combinator Winter 2026, six firm logos on the home page, and five case studies: Riviera Partners, Paragon Legal, FirstLook Partners, a European HR firm and a W2 staffing firm (1,000+ interviews a week).

Vela connects to common tools but has no partner programme where other companies build on it. It works with Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Slack and Teams. I found no marketplace or partner page, and the home FAQ's answer on an API did not load.
One customer's use does not help another customer. Product description. The only network-like effect is that candidates and clients on a thread get to know Vela.
It is software only. Nothing physical is involved.

Vela uses human executive assistants to guarantee accuracy, so costs grow with customers. It is also a small company. The /tldr page says accuracy is 'backed by certified Executive Assistants'. YC lists about 15 staff. Support is email only, weekdays 9am to 6pm.

sections.title: What Spott is, and who it is for
sections.text: Spott is one tool for recruitment agencies and in-house recruiters. It joins an ATS (your candidates, jobs and placements) with a CRM (your companies, contacts and deals). You add a job, and Spott finds and ranks the best candidates from your own database. It then follows them through a pipeline and records the placement and fee. Each person is saved once (as a candidate, a contact or both), so notes, emails and calls stay on one record. It replaces typing in CVs, cleaning duplicates, writing meeting notes and building reports by hand.

sections.title: How it works, step by step
sections.text:
The work goes in six steps, from job to placement. It can also start with a CRM deal. Automatic actions and AI help at every step.
Often it starts in the CRM: a company, a contact, a deal. A won deal becomes a job.
Behind every step: automatic actions when a person moves stage, and AI working on every record.
steps: Add the job and link the client company. Paste or upload the job description (link, PDF or Word). Add what you are looking for and your intake notes.

Run AI Matching: first filters that must be met, then ranked wishes, each person scored 0-100 with a reason. Or advertise the job, or add CVs by upload, email, extension or CSV. Duplicates merge by themselves.
Drag people through your own stages on a board. Write notes, let the Note Taker write up meetings, send follow-up campaigns and score interviews with scorecards.
Send them by email, as an AI-written Word shortlist (names can be hidden), or through the client portal where the client leaves comments. Book interviews from the calendar.
Choose a type (Contingent, Retained or Contract). Record the fee or rates, dates and splits (they must add up to 100%). Send an invoice draft to Xero.
The dashboard, targets and reports update from your activity, and you can export to Excel. Automations can close the job, send consent emails and create tasks.

sections.title: Features and how they work
cols: What it does, in simple words
rows: Reads up to 1,000 CVs at once, even scans and photos. If there are fewer than 20, you check the details first. Drop them straight into a job stage or a list.
Forward PDF or Word CVs to cv@spott.io (up to 250 per email). You become the main contact. If a CV fails, the error is emailed back.
If you upload a newer CV, only the changes are added. Spott also finds emails, phone numbers and LinkedIn links (costs credits) and keeps profiles up to date.
Import CSV or Excel files; AI matches your columns to Spott fields. A Chrome extension adds people from LinkedIn. Email, phone and LinkedIn link must be unique, so duplicates are caught.
Search with AND, OR and NOT. Filter by job title, experience, place (radius, area, ZIP), pay, last contact, reason for rejection and consent. Save your favourite searches as Views.
Write something like "React developer, 5+ years, California" and Spott turns it into filters.
Describe the person you want, or start from a job. Filters narrow the list and AI ranks it 0-100. Accept, mark as reviewed, shortlist or share.
The same AI, started from a job. Results appear as they are found, as cards or a table, with history and export. It can also match one candidate to many jobs, or find people near a company.
Change a field, add to a list, job or campaign (up to 9,999 at a time), make a Word shortlist or send bulk email slowly.
Create a job by hand, from a link or from a file. Each job has tabs: Overview, Matching, Candidates, Campaigns, Advertising, Applicants, Portal, Files, Notes and Tasks, plus a board of stages.
Post to the Spott job board, LinkedIn, Broadbean, idibu or VDAB. People who apply are scored by AI against the job.
The client sees a shortlist and comments live. AI drafts interview scorecards from your criteria and rates the answers from your interview notes.
Boards for deals. A deal can turn into a job. Adding a contact reuses a person you already have. Company details can be looked up. Group records in Lists.
Three types: Contingent, Retained (paid in steps) and Contract (rates and margin). Fee splits, your own forms, and options for drop-out, change to permanent and extend.
Approved timesheets and fees become invoices. Drafts go to Xero and the status comes back. See booked revenue, expected starters and gross profit.
Gmail or Outlook, WhatsApp and SMS in one place. Reply, schedule a send, use templates, get AI drafts, or send bulk emails one person at a time.
Sync your calendar and share booking links. A bot joins Zoom, Teams or Meet, writes everything down in any language, and gives you notes in 2 to 5 minutes.
Phone calls (Aircall, RingCentral, Ringover) are written out and mined for updates. Tasks have due dates and links. Notes can use templates.
Steps can be email, or a manual LinkedIn, call, WhatsApp or task step. Fill in names with variables or AI text. A campaign stops when someone replies. Limit: 125 emails a day per mailbox.
Bulk email with open and click tracking, an unsubscribe link and a block list. You need a verified sending domain.
Ask questions or give tasks on one record or the whole workspace. Changes need your approval. It searches emails, notes and calls, remembers your preferences and runs saved Skills.
Write one instruction and AI fills a field for every record (1 credit per value).
About 28 triggers. Actions: send email, create a task, change a field, add a note, close job adverts. Use If/Then/Else, waits and AI conditions, and check the run logs.
Boxes for numbers, lists, pipelines and charts. Targets are spread over working days. Funnels, time in each stage, and Excel export.
Phone systems, job boards, Xero, DocuSign, Creditsafe and SAP Fieldglass. A REST API and webhooks. An MCP server lets Claude and ChatGPT work with Spott.
User permissions, two-step login and GDPR consent. 1,000 credits per user each month. iOS and Android app for search, notes and meeting recording.

sections.title: The AI parts of Spott
sections.text: AI is part of the core, not an extra. It reads your own records (notes, CVs, work history and call transcripts) and helps in seven areas.
rows: Ranks your whole database from 0 to 100 for a job, using your notes, work history and call transcripts. Turns job text into filters and ranked wishes. Explains every score, and you can press thumbs up or down on each reason to correct it. The AI Search tab finds people from a plain description.
Reads CVs into profiles, merges re-uploaded CVs and shows what changed, matches CSV columns, finds emails, phones and LinkedIn links, fills AI fields and scores people who apply.
Answers questions, searches emails, notes and calls by meaning, writes email drafts, and creates or moves records after you approve. Remembers your preferences and runs saved Skills.
The Note Taker joins meetings, writes everything down in any language and makes notes from your templates. Call transcripts give suggested profile updates and tasks.
Job descriptions, campaign emails for each person, AI blocks in email templates, interview scorecards and ratings, formatted CVs and Word shortlists.
AI conditions, for example "candidate has 5+ years of React". People who apply are scored against the role.
The MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot search and update Spott. Each user signs in with their own account.
sections.after: Control and limits: admins can switch AI features on or off. Templates and prompts guide what the AI writes. Every AI change to your records needs your approval. Only Ask Spott can read email, and no AI reads WhatsApp. AI conditions are judgments, not exact checks. AI columns and finding contact details cost credits.

sections.title: What Flynt is, and who it is for
sections.text: Flynt helps recruiters and agencies win new clients. You tell it which jobs and companies you want. Every day a Flynt "agent" (an automatic helper) looks for companies that are hiring. It finds the person who does the hiring, checks their work email, gives the lead a score from 0 to 100, and writes a personal email for you. Your leads, emails and replies all stay in one place: a CRM (a list of your leads) and an inbox.

sections.title: How it works, Part 1: finding leads
sections.text:
Each time the agent runs, your leads pass through seven stages. Flynt shows how many records survived each stage and, under "Why N dropped", why the rest were removed.
The agent does this by itself every day (numbers from a real run).
steps: 10 have the job title you want

sections.title: How it works, Part 2: reaching out
sections.text: Starts when you connect a campaign and your own mailbox.
steps: New leads are added to your campaign
A personal email for each lead
Up to 8 emails, from your mailbox, slowly
Arrive in the Inbox with labels
Move the lead to Won, Lost and so on

sections.title: How it works, step by step
sections.text:
1. Set up an agent. Pick the job titles you want (up to 5), the places (up to 6), the industries, and the size of company. You can also block words you do not want.
2. The agent runs every day. It finds jobs posted in the last 24 hours and groups them by company. It keeps only companies that fit your size, industry and place, and skips recruitment agencies.
3. It finds the right person. At each company it looks for the person who decides on hiring, such as a head of product. It then finds a work email and checks that it is real.
4. It scores each lead. The score goes from 0 to 100. Under it, Flynt explains in plain words why the lead matched or did not match.
5. You send emails. Connect the agent to a campaign. Flynt writes up to 8 emails for each lead and sends them slowly, in business hours. Nothing is sent until you connect your own mailbox.
6. You follow the replies. Replies come into the Inbox with labels. You move each lead through simple stages and track deal value on a board.

sections.title: Features and how they work
cols: What it does, in simple words
rows: Finds companies that just posted a job you care about. It runs by itself every day at the time you choose. In the trial it gives up to 5 leads a day for 7 days. "Run Now" starts an extra run (3 extra runs in the trial). If too few leads are found, Flynt loosens your filters a little. If your search is too narrow, that day's run is skipped.
Finds companies that just raised money or were bought, before they announce jobs. Available on Pro, Growth and Scale, or as an add-on on Starter.

Upload one candidate's CV and Flynt sets up the agent for you. It then writes each email around that candidate. You need one agent per candidate. The trial allows 3 uploads a day. (This comes from Flynt's chat helper; I did not try it.)
Five tabs: Agent Info (name, schedule), Jobs (titles, places, industries, full-time or remote), Companies (size, words to exclude), People (which job titles to contact), Campaign (where leads go).

Open any run to see all seven stages and how many records passed. "Why N dropped" gives reasons, such as: 14 companies in the wrong industry, 6 were recruitment agencies, 17 people with the wrong job title, 3 with no working email. "Edit targeting" takes you to the setting to change.
Choose the daily run time and switch it on or off. You can send new leads straight into a campaign, or only have Flynt write the messages so you send them yourself by email or phone.

Put six things in order of importance: the job they hire for, the manager's location, seniority, company size, industry, and recent funding. You can add a note, such as "score newly promoted managers higher".
A score from 0 to 100 with a short summary, the reasons it is a good match, and a list of each point with a tick or a gap. You can press thumbs up or thumbs down to tell Flynt what you think.

Opens beside the list. It shows the person, their company, the job being advertised, a place for the email Flynt wrote, and a history of what happened. You also get their email, LinkedIn link and a "Reveal phone number" button. Company news needs a paid plan.
Free in the trial: click "Reveal phone number" on a lead. On a paid plan, an add-on finds about 900 numbers a month for $189 per agent on Starter.

A campaign can have up to 8 emails (6 by default, sent on days 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 and 14; you can change the gaps). You do not write them. Flynt writes each one for each lead. You choose the tone (friendly, direct, professional or advising), add your own instructions, make a second version to compare, and preview examples. Check buttons test for rule and spam problems.

Emails go from your own mailbox, on weekdays 9 to 5 (Eastern time), with a 10-minute gap between emails. Flynt sets a daily limit. You can slow the start for a new mailbox, set a minimum score, and the best leads are contacted first.
Shows how many leads were queued, contacted, opened, clicked, replied and became deals, and how each email step performed. You can rename, copy or delete a campaign.
Sends connection requests and messages in the same plan as your emails. Locked in the trial; included on paid plans.
Folders: Inbox, Sent, Reminders and Unread. Label replies as Lead, Not a lead, Interested, Not now or Not interested. Filter by campaign, or search by words, sender or receiver.

Search by name, email or company. Filter by date, by status, by what happened to the email (not contacted, opened, replied, bounced, unsubscribed) or by score group (Excellent 90-100, Great 75-89, Good 50-74, Poor below 50). Choose columns and download a CSV file.
Nine ready-made statuses: Lead, Interested, Meeting Booked, Meeting Completed, Won, Lost, No Show, Wrong Person and Not Interested. You can also create your own labels.
A board with one column per status. Each card shows a deal value (the default is $5,000, which you can change) with totals for open and won deals.
Connect a Gmail or other mailbox, or order new website names (.com or .org) and mailboxes from Flynt's "My email orders" page.
Block companies or industries, skip companies you contacted in the last 3 months, get emails for new leads and good replies, and connect Slack.

The Copilot chat answers questions from Flynt's help pages. Quick Start has 6 short videos: welcome, intro, agent setup, leads, campaigns with email setup, and Gmail setup. Help pages and support links are included.

sections.title: What Atlas is, and who it is for
sections.text: Atlas is the one place where a recruitment agency runs its whole business. It is an ATS (a system that tracks candidates and jobs) and a CRM (a system that tracks clients and sales deals) in one tool, with AI built in. A recruiter normally jumps between a spreadsheet, an email inbox, LinkedIn, a calendar and a notes app. Atlas puts candidates, clients, jobs, emails, meetings, tasks and fees together, so nothing is lost and no one types the same thing twice. It is made for recruiters, agencies and in-house hiring teams. The problem it solves: too much manual admin and scattered data. The AI writes notes, drafts emails, scores candidates and answers questions about your data.

sections.title: How it works, step by step
sections.text:
Atlas covers two jobs that recruiters do every week: winning clients (Part A) and filling the roles those clients give you (Part B).
Part A, win a client (business development): Company, Contact, Opportunity (tracked in 7 stages), Campaign (emails, LinkedIn, calls, to-dos), Meeting (AI records and writes notes), Job (the client gives you a role to fill).
Part B, fill the job (recruiting): Job post, AI criteria (scoring rules and personas), Find people (search your own database), Pipeline (7 stages), Client portal (a board or a one-page report), Placement (hired, and the fee is logged).
steps: Create a company (Client or Target) and add the people there. A person can be a Candidate, a Contact, or both.
Create an Opportunity. It moves through Identified, Pursuing, Initial request, Late Stage, then Converted or Lost. Outreach campaigns sit inside it.
You need only a role name and a company. Paste a job description and Atlas AI turns it into screening rules and three search profiles.
Search your database and add people to the job. Move them through the pipeline from Sourcing to Hired.
Campaigns send multi-step outreach. AI can draft each message. Meeting AI records calls and writes the notes for you.
Share progress with the client, log the fee when someone is placed, and watch team numbers in Analytics.

sections.title: Features and how they work
cols: What it does, in simple words
rows: A morning view with today's meetings, tasks, interviews, your jobs and campaign numbers. A timeline shows your focus. Buttons: "Prep for next meeting" and "Recap last call".

Opens beside the list. Tabs: Overview, Jobs, Interviews, Files (resume upload), Compensation, Details, Activities, Atlas AI and Insights. You can send email, book a meeting, add a task or add the person to a list or a job.

"New search" has 12 filter groups: Role, Company, Location, Keywords, Profile info, Education, Seniority, Function, Industry, Compensation, Profile depth, Communication. There is also "use AI text to filter", saved views, and "Past assessments". Import takes Excel or CSV (or pasted table) for Candidates, Prospects or Clients. Export and column choice are at the top. The "Get Chrome extension" button (in Settings menu) installs an add-on that saves people and job leads from web pages in one click.
A pop-up box to find any company, candidate, client or prospect. It lists recent items with Ctrl 1 to 4 shortcuts and has quick buttons for "Create task" and "Schedule meeting".
Each job has Dashboard, Overview, Job description, Sourcing, Candidates, Client portal and Financials. Overview holds client, owner, team, place, salary notes and files.

Paste a job description, then "Generate criteria" to make scoring rules. Sourcing makes three search profiles (for example Fintech Python Core), each as "Filters only" or "Filters + criteria". "AI redraft" rewrites the description.
Default stages: Sourcing, Internal IV, Presented, Client IV, Offer, Hired and Rejected, each with sub-steps (for example Scheduled, Sent, Signed, Past probation). You can edit them in Settings.
When a candidate reaches Hired (Signed, Started, Past probation), the placement shows in Permanent. You then add a fee on the job's Financials tab and link the placement.

Two ways to share with your client, each with a live preview. Kanban board: choose stages to show (Presented to Hired), whether they see LinkedIn, references and resume download, and which columns. Executive report: a cover page with client logo, colour and summary, longlist and rejected sections, and optional automatic reporting.

Company page shows contacts, people, jobs, placements, offices, files and terms of business. Contact page shows active jobs, placements, meetings and "float" candidates (people you offer to a client).

Two kinds: Business opportunity, and Candidate driven (built from one candidate). Tabs: Notes, Overview, Outreach, Prospects, Companies, Leads. An AI "conversion probability" panel starts once prospect activity exists. A Playbook page holds your sales method.

Candidate outreach: find people for one specific job. General: send to a list of contacts. Candidate led: introduce one candidate to several contacts. Opportunity: a campaign inside a sales opportunity. Each is a sequence of steps with a delay: Email, LinkedIn connection, InMail, Phone call or To-do. "AI draft" writes a step, "Send test emails" previews it. Overview shows added, opened, replied, interested and presented.

Paste a Meet, Teams or Zoom link, or pick a calendar event, and the AI notetaker joins, records and writes notes. You can also email notes@recruitwithatlas.com. "Create meeting" has attendees, "Resolve with AI" for dates, an Interview toggle, job link and "Draft with AI". Self-scheduling links let people book you.

Tasks have three tabs: General, Candidate outreach and BD outreach, with due date, priority and recipient. Lists group people (default type: Candidate) and can be Private, Team or Company shared (view or edit).

Placements and Fees tables (by fee or by fee split), with export. Performance ranks consultants by fees. The job Financials tab adds a fee: type, currency, amount, status (starts as Projected), dates, notes for the invoice, several fee earners with roles, and a linked placement.

Five tabs. Activity: campaign, interview and time-to-hire numbers per person. Team (needs a team set up). Consultant: target cards. Analytics: type what you want to see and AI builds a dashboard. Active candidates: your live list.

"Magic credits" pay for AI actions: 100 per month free, 2,000 more for GBP 20 per month, or a 2,000 pack for GBP 29. "AI Agent instructions" set your writing style for candidates, reports, campaigns and interviews. "Skills" are your own saved AI instructions.

Users, job roles, permissions, custom attributes, blocked emails and domains, approvals, Signable docs (e-sign), terminology and design. Rules: auto-delete applicants after a set time and who may edit stages.

WhatsApp is on. Xero (accounting), Timesheet Portal, Claude, phone systems (RingCentral, RingOver, 8x8, AirCall, Devyce), job boards (Idibu, Broadbean, LogicMelon) and CoRecruit meeting notes can be connected. Optional modules: GDPR notices, public job page, contractor contracts, end clients. The Help button opens a chat with an AI agent and the Atlas team.

sections.title: The AI parts of Atlas
sections.text: What is the main AI-native part of Atlas? These are the AI features the report highlights.
rows: A chat box available on every page. You ask in plain words, for example "Summarize my open tasks", and it answers from the data already in your Atlas: the task, its due date, its priority and a link to the person. It can also read your emails and notes, so you do not search for things by hand.
Paste a job description into a job, click "Generate criteria", and Atlas turns the text into a scoring checklist. It is then used to judge how well each candidate fits the role.
"Generate personas" reads the same text and suggests three different kinds of ideal candidate to search for. Each comes with a short reason and can be used as "Filters only" or "Filters + criteria".
An AI notetaker can join a Meet, Teams or Zoom call, listen, and write the notes for you. You can invite it from any meeting in your calendar with one click.

"AI draft" writes a campaign message, "Draft with AI" and "Resolve with AI" help fill in the meeting form, "use AI text to filter" turns a sentence into People search filters, the Analytics box builds a dashboard from what you type, and the "Atlas AI" tab sits on each candidate profile.
